note: Source's "to be precise" qualifier is dropped.
replacement: As for the rest of life, with its so-called "experiences," which of us takes a serious enough interest in it? Or has enough time? I fear that in dealing with such matters we are never properly present: to be precise, our heart is not in it, and certainly not our ear. We are like a man lost in divine distraction, or sunk in the seas of his own soul, in whose ear the clock has just thundered its twelve strokes of noon with all its force. He suddenly wakes up and asks himself, "What in fact has just struck?" In the same way we sometimes rub our puzzled ears afterwards and ask, in complete astonishment and complete embarrassment, "What have we in fact just lived through?" And further, "Who are we in fact?" Then we count, after they have struck, as I have explained, all twelve throbbing beats of the clock of our experience, of our life, of our being — ah! — and we count wrong in the attempt. Of necessity we remain strangers to ourselves; we do not understand ourselves; we are bound to be mistaken about ourselves. For us the motto holds good for all eternity: "Each one is the farthest away from himself" — as far as ourselves are concerned, we are not "knowers."
